sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Leveraged Buyout Acquisition Syndicate and Special Purpose Co

stage_1.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate General Partner / anchor Limited Partner
stage_1.issuing_entity: Official Trade Register or competent authority of country of origin
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (notably by the Law of 23 July 2016 on Special Limited Partnerships); Articles 101-1 to 101-21 (SCSp); Articles 13-15 of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) operated under the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified declaration of registration (déclaration en vue de l'immatriculation) filed with the RCS together with the partnership agreement (contrat de société) and identification dossiers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital and no mandatory paid-up capital or escrow account requirement for an SCSp; capital may be nominal and is determined solely by the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriptions to the partnership interests of the SCSp, as reflected in the subscription schedule attached hereto, are hereby approved and accepted in accordance with the partnership agreement dated [date]. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, subject to notification to the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as manager (gérant) with sole power to bind the SCSp within the scope of the partnership purpose. RESOLVED, that bank mandate is granted to the manager and [Name] as co-signatory for the opening of the operational account. RESOLVED, that RCS filing, publication, and legalization formalities are delegated to [law firm].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Partnership Agreement (Acte Constitutif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (notarial deed optional unless real property is contributed); private deed executed by the general partner and initial limited partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SCSp partnership agreement in Luxembourg law format, including corporate name, registered office address, purpose (leveraged buyout acquisition syndicate), capital and interest classes, identity of general and limited partners, manager appointment clause, and profit-sharing terms. Execute by all initial partners; notarization is recommended for bank opening and future legalization efficiency.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of general partner and initial limited partners
Proof of address of each partner
CV and legalization documents for corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is queried, amend the draft to comply with legal form requirements and re-execute; no registry penalty applies prior to submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate current account in the SCSp name for receipt of subscription proceeds and future syndicated loan wire transactions. Execute bank mandate per the first board resolution; deposit agreed initial capital (no statutory minimum) and obtain a certificate of block if deemed necessary by the bank's internal policy for the buyout SPV.
required_dossiers: First board resolution / written resolutions of general partner
AML/KYC file of the SCSp and economic owners
Bank account opening form and mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the bank requests enhanced due diligence for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier, furnish a full corporate ownership chart and source-of-funds declaration; re-submit within the bank's KYC remediation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via the eJustice electronic filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic registration application through the eJustice portal, attaching the partnership agreement, certified declaration of registration, identity documents, and proof of commercial address. After validation, the RCS assigns the corporate registration number and issues the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of manager and partners
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incomplete data, cure by filing an amending declaration via the same portal within 5 working days; register any discrepant corporate purpose language against the ISIC 6499 scope description.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Official Electronic Recueil des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically publishes the registration notice in RESA after a successful filing. Verify the published notice for accuracy of the SCSp name, registered office, general partner identity, and manager powers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a correction of the published notice via the RCS helpdesk if any disclosed information is erroneous; the request must be filed within 30 days of publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Registration and Tax Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers; Administration des contributions directes for registration of the taxable entity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial owner declaration with the RBE within 30 days of RCS registration, identifying the ultimate natural persons holding or controlling the SPV. Concurrently, complete taxpayer registration with the Luxembourg direct tax administration and register for Luxembourg VAT only if taxable supplies are made (generally inactive).
required_dossiers: Identification documents of ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For an RBE discrepancy notice, update the ownership chart and file a corrected declaration within 15 days to avoid administrative fines; tax registration is processed automatically upon RCS data transmission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Directorate General for Industry (Ministère de l'Économie). No industrial operating permit is required for a pure private equity buyout SPV (ISIC 6499 / NAICS 525910).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - the SPV is a non-regulated financial holding vehicle; no commercial, manufacturing, or financial sector operating license is required. A CSSF confirmation of non-regulated status may be obtained voluntarily.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category C (administrative office use only; no physical installation, construction, or industrial process triggering a full EIA study or separate environmental registration).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no wastewater or VOC discharge points exist for the SPV's passive financial activity; general municipal solid waste management rules under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste apply to leased office premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificat de sécurité incendie) for the registered office premises is required by the communal authority; occupational health and workplace clearance is mandatory under the Labor Code and supervised by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); no structural load inspection applies for an office-only SPV.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg Inland Revenue) for direct taxes, municipal business tax, net wealth tax and withholding taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and stamp duties. Primary digital portals: MyGuichet.lu (Professionnels / eSpace professionnel), the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/eJustice) platform, and the AEDT e-TVA portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an LU SCSp (Special LP): (1) execute the limited partnership agreement before a Luxembourg notary and file the instrument for registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) using the eJustice platform; (2) upon RCS registration, the entity obtains its unique Luxembourg business identification number (numéro d'identification) and RCS registration reference (format B + 6 or more digits); (3) for VAT, the SCSp, as an economic operator, must file a domestic VAT registration form (formulaire TVA 800/801) with the AEDT, which assigns a Luxembourg VAT number in the standard format LU + 8 digits; a foreign entity not established in Luxembourg has a mandatory registration obligation without turnover threshold when it performs taxable transactions in Luxembourg; (4) if the SCSp needs to declare Luxembourg-source income, claim tax treaty benefits on behalf of partners, or satisfy local withholding obligations, the ACD opens a tax file and designates the competent bureau d'imposition of the registered seat; (5) a regulated alternative investment vehicle (RAIF/SIF/SICAR) shall submit the notification to the CSSF, which does not replace AEDT/ACD registration for fiscal purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg. The fiscal transparency of the SCSp is statutorily fixed by Article 5bis of the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as amended); the transparency regime applies mandatorily for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax, and no election to be taxed at entity level is available under domestic law. Alternative pass-through structuring may be achieved through a civil co-ownership (indivision) or a dormant partnership (société en participation). Hybrid mismatch arrangements are governed by the ATAD transposition (Law of 21 December 2018, as amended), applying the deduction/no-inclusion, dual inclusion income, importation and branch mismatch rules to cross-border equity and finance structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 of annual taxable turnover, exclusive of VAT, for small and medium undertakings established in Luxembourg; the threshold does not apply to non-established foreign businesses, which must register for VAT before carrying out taxable transactions in Luxembourg; voluntary registration is available below the threshold but is impracticable for an exempt financial private-equity SPV because input VAT recovery on exempt financial services is denied.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory B2B e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or transaction-based VAT reporting is currently implemented in Luxembourg. Since 18 April 2023, invoices addressed to the Luxembourg central government and public-sector bodies must be issued as structured PEPPOL e-invoices (EN 16931). For B2B transactions, e-invoicing is permitted by mutual acceptance of the parties; no AEDT pre-clearance or certification of invoices is required. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) initiative may introduce mandatory e-invoicing and digital reporting after 2030; Luxembourg has as of the date of this dossier no enacted law imposing such a regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating under Article 41 of the Luxembourg VAT Law applies to supplies of goods dispatched or transported by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf to a destination outside the European Union; the supplier must hold transport and customs evidence establishing that the goods physically left the EU. Intra-EU B2B supplies are zero-rated under Article 42 when the customer's EU VAT registration number is valid at the time of supply, the goods are transported out of Luxembourg to another Member State, and the EC Sales List is timely filed. Services: the place of supply for B2B services is the customer's place of establishment under Article 14, so services to non-EU investors, dividend streams, disposal gains and loan interest of a private-equity buyout SPV are either outside Luxembourg VAT or exempt financial services; no zero-rating application is required for such off-shore passive income. Substantiation for any zero-rated goods export requires the formal export declaration accepted by customs and the commercial transport/remittance documentation set; no statutory FX repatriation deadline is imposed by Luxembourg VAT law, but the standard commercial threshold of 180 days for inward remittance evidence is applied in practice by financing banks and tax auditors.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Declaration / SAD) lodged in the electronic export system (AES / EU CS) and released by Luxembourg or another Member State customs office
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note evidencing the physical transportation out of the European Union
Commercial Invoice and export packing list
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire evidence (e.g., SWIFT MT103) proving receipt of export proceeds from the non-EU buyer
Where available, proof of importation into the destination country (customs entry certificate, import declaration or foreign customs stamp)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may conduct post-clearance audits and requires the complete export evidence bundle to be retained for at least six years. Where zero-rating is improperly claimed or the documentation is untraceable, the tax authority reassesses the supply at the standard 17% VAT rate, claws back any input VAT previously deducted on the associated costs, and applies default interest at the rate of 0.6% per month from the due date of the tax. Administrative penalties range from EUR 250 up to 20% of the tax evaded in good-faith cases, and rise to up to 100% of the tax in bad-faith cases. Fraudulent export arrangements may also attract criminal sanctions under Articles 53 to 59 of the Luxembourg VAT Law and Articles 393 et seq. of the Luxembourg Criminal Code, including imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000, with joint and several liability of the managing partners of the SCSp under the charging and collection provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: La Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); administrative supervision of treasury, banking, and FX compliance also rests with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls on capital account or current account transactions. Profit remittance by an SCSp is limited only by partnership law and the Limited Partnership Agreement distribution waterfall; there is no profit remittance approval or conversion permit. Practical hurdles are limited to AML/KYC evidence, tax transparency, and substance documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion percentage, and no statutory repatriation deadline. Export receipts and other cross-border receivables may be held in foreign currency, but resident banks must report cross-border flows to the BCL for monetary and balance-of-payments statistics.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BGL BNP Paribas S.A. Luxembourg Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-low viability. An EU-authorised electronic money institution can provide ancillary euro accounts and payment initiation, but cannot safely support acquisition escrow, syndicated loan drawdowns, or material FX settlements. Offshore or non-EU digital EMIs are legally unusable because they lack the required Luxembourg/EEA payment institution passport and access to TARGET2; such accounts would create regulatory and bank product governance exposure. The SCSp must use a CSSF-supervised credit institution for its primary treasury rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted in Luxembourg when CSSF-compliant video identification, digital signature, and certified document procedures are used. For a private equity buyout SCSp, the bank will normally require a CDD interview with the authorised signatory of the general partner and with each material UBO; the Luxembourg-resident independent director may serve as the local interface. Physical appearance by every director is not mandatory, but a physical meeting may be required where the beneficial ownership chain is complex or involves non-EU offshore jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp general partner and UBO structure include multiple non-EU entities, trusts, or unregulated foundations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current extract from the Luxembourg business register, UBO declaration filed with the RBE register, executed limited partnership agreement, notarised resolutions of the general partner, ownership waterfall to natural persons, passports, proof of legal existence, and curriculum vitae or directorship evidence for all material controllers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital call or subscription payment originates from a high-risk jurisdiction without visible economic rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements, executed subscription agreement, capital call notices, source-of-funds letters, tax returns for the last three years, professional advisory engagement letters, commercial substance memorandum, and an independent legal opinion or audit trail on the underlying investment purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party funding or circular cross-investor transfers trigger layering or unusual transaction flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated escrow and correspondent account documentation, notary or payment-agent instruction letters, full payment chain ledger, signed AML counsel confirmation, investor-to-SCSp contractual chain, and non-recourse or equity contribution documentation if transaction leverage is present.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use architecturally compliant SWIFT MT103 wires from the investor bank to the SCSp operational account. Remittance information must reference the LEI of the SCSp, the executed subscription agreement, and the capital call date. Include a clear purpose description such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - SCSp EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION'. There is no BCL exchange-control approval, but the receiving Luxembourg bank must report the cross-border transaction under BCL balance-of-payments statistics and verify the source of funds. Credit is effective on TARGET2 if received before the 16:00 Luxembourg settlement cutoff.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for the final cash purchase price, settlement of bridge financing, and vendor payments; use SWIFT MT202 COV for third-party cover payments when needed. For the acquisition of a target with an assurance requirement, issue or procure a confirmed commercial letter of credit under UCP600, payable at sight, or use a dual-signature escrow release instruction. For euro-denominated operational disbursements, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer provides final settlement in seconds; non-EUR disbursements are cleared via SWIFT correspondent banking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX vanilla European call and put options
FX swap (short-date swap) for treasury sweeps
Cross-currency interest rate swap aligned to acquisition debt service

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RBE Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership Data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, at any time between 1 January and 31 December; any change in beneficial ownership (including transfers of partnership interests) must be filed within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 500–EUR 1,250 (doubled upon recidivism); non-compliance persisting beyond 3 months after formal notice triggers court-ordered suspension of voting rights and profit-distribution rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS Deposit of Annual Accounts (via eCDF) – applicable only if the SCSp qualifies as a large undertaking or the LPA elects publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end (e.g., by 31 July following a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 5,000 under the Law of 19 December 2020; repeated failure exposes the general partner (gérant) to personal liability and court-ordered compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Partnership Income Tax Return (allocation of SCSp income/loss to partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year filers: due by the ACD reminder date, typically 31 December of the year following the tax year; e-filing extension generally applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax; late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 for persistent failure after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register Audit and Partner Approval of Annual Accounts (internal secretarial review)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None – registers maintained at the registered office and certified by the general partner (gérant); submitted to partners for approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after financial year-end, prior to the annual partners' meeting unless the LPA provides otherwise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct state penalty; deficient registers create evidentiary and liability exposure in disputes, AML/KYC reviews, insolvency proceedings, and succession scenarios.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: SCSp is exempt from statutory audit and annual accounts publication by default (Article 2055, Law of 10 August 1915). Mandatory audit arises if the SCSp is classified as a large undertaking under the Law of 19 December 2020 (balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average headcount > 50 for two consecutive years), or when the LPA, a third-party lender, or a fund regulation (RAIF/SIF/SICAR) requires an independent auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan comptable normalisé, Law of 19 December 2020 on undertakings transparency). IFRS as adopted in the EU is permitted for consolidated or voluntary financial statements. Bookkeeping is compulsory under the Luxembourg Code de commerce.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Mandatory annual RBE confirmation once per calendar year (deadline 31 December). Every transfer of partnership interests must be recorded immediately in the on-site register of partners and declared to the RBE within 30 days; the annual confirmation certifies that recorded beneficial ownership remains accurate and complete.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Registre des Associés Commanditaires)
Minute Book (Procès-Verbaux des décisions des associés)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,200–8,500 per annum (EUR 2,000–7,500) for registered office, corporate domiciliation, and company secretarial services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–25,000 per annum; typical buyout SPV audit engagement USD 7,000–15,000 (EUR 6,500–13,500) depending on transaction complexity and group consolidation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% composite headline rate in Luxembourg City: national CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT (1.19%) + municipal business tax 6.75%. The SCSp is fiscally transparent and therefore bears no entity-level CIT on ordinary results.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective CIT at SCSp level due to full fiscal transparency (ACD Circular LIR n. 14/4); distributions to partners are not subject to Luxembourg dividend WHT; corporate partners benefit from the participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; municipal business tax is not triggered for wealth-management or pure buyout-holding activities; net wealth tax is assessed at partner level, not SCSp level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (statutory unlimited carryforward under Art. 114 LIR; no 5-year statutory cap; anti-abuse reassessment may apply where more than 25% of the partnership interests change hands without business purpose)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 541 - Declaration pour l'impot sur le revenu des collectivites, together with the partnership allocation schedules and the loss carryforward annex; filed electronically via the MyGuichet.lu portal (ACD e-filing service of the Luxembourg Inland Revenue) or on paper at the competent Luxembourg tax office (Bureau d'imposition).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; CIT and municipal business tax prepayments are settled in four quarterly instalments due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December of the current tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., FY 2024 return due on 31 December 2025); the ACD may grant individual extensions upon reasoned request, but extensions do not suspend default interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the SCSp, RCS registration number, Luxembourg tax identification number (NIF), registered office address, date of incorporation, and identification of the general partner (associe gerant).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident general partner or non-resident limited partner must disclose its foreign tax identification number, confirm whether it maintains a Luxembourg permanent establishment, and appoint a Luxembourg tax representative for service of process and correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss summary: gross investment income, acquisition financing costs, interest expense, management fees, guarantee fees and other deductible operating charges of the buyout SPV.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all cross-border related-party financing at arm's length rates and attach contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for intercompany loans and fee arrangements exceeding EUR 1 million equivalent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income or loss among the general partner and the limited partners, including the carried interest waterfall, preferred return and loss sharing ratios per the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner provide the full legal name, jurisdiction of tax residence, tax identification number and percentage entitlement; this schedule underpins treaty relief claims and proves that Luxembourg-source income is allocated to the partner rather than to a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of available ordinary losses brought forward, current-year utilisation, and remaining balance for future allocation to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claiming foreign tax credits on Luxembourg-source allocated income must reproduce this computation in their home jurisdiction and retain the ACD-received filing evidence for credit purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex 2 - Partner tax status and exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of partner-level exemption regimes, including the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive participation status, DTA residence article, and any claim for relief at source on Luxembourg allocable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach valid tax residence certificates (TRC) issued by the partner's home tax authority and a beneficial ownership statement; the TRC must be current, certified, and translated into French or German if not issued in an EU official language.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on assessed tax (Art. 155 LIR); additional coercive fines from EUR 250 to EUR 2,500; default interest accrues at 0.6% per month on overdue tax; willful non-filing or false returns escalate to criminal tax fraud under Art. 1754 AO with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on distributions by an SCSp: as a fiscally transparent vehicle lacking legal personality, profit distributions are not dividends and no Luxembourg withholding tax is levied. For comparison, a Luxembourg corporation would attract the statutory 15% dividend WHT (Art. 146 LIR), reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or most DTAs where a 10% plus participation is held for 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The SCSp's general partner files Form 270 (withholding tax declaration) only when a Luxembourg-resident withholding event occurs; non-resident partners must submit a current TRC, a beneficial ownership declaration, and a statement of the percentage participation to the ACD to invoke DTA relief at source or to claim a refund of any Luxembourg WHT withheld; treaty access requires the SCSp and its partners to satisfy the substance and beneficial-ownership standards; the DTA rate for corporate partners with a 10%-plus holding is generally 0% to 5%, otherwise 15%; disputes are resolved through mutual agreement procedure under the applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest on shareholder loans and third-party acquisition debt: 0% Luxembourg WHT (no domestic withholding on interest). Royalties for IP, software and brand licences paid by the SCSp: 0% domestic WHT. Treaty caps typically range from 0% to 5% for both interest and royalties, subject to beneficial ownership and substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg prescribes no fixed statutory Local File or Master File monetary threshold; the arm's length standard under Art. 56 LIR and Circular 56/1 imposes contemporaneous documentation on all intra-group transactions. Mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting applies to MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Prudent SPV practice: maintain a Local File when intercompany financing or management fees exceed EUR 1 million and a Master File when intra-group revenue exceeds EUR 5 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation statute; substance is enforced through the ATAD-derived GAAR (Art. 6 ACI), Art. 56 LIR, anti-hybrid rules, and the ACD's anti-abuse ruling practice. The SCSp must demonstrate genuine business substance: physical office, board or general partner meetings held in Luxembourg, local decision-making, Luxembourg bank accounts, complete accounting records, and proportionate staffing; failure to prove substance may result in denial of pass-through treatment, treaty access, and the 0% distribution characterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to file Form 541, concealment of partnership income, falsified allocation schedules, fictitious expenses, destroyed accounting records, or deliberately inconsistent reporting between the SCSp and its partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under Art. 1754 Luxembourg General Tax Law (AO): imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000; civil reassessment of tax evaded plus a 10% evasion surcharge and default interest at 0.6% per month; loss of payment grace periods and immediate enforceability of tax claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner, and the directors of a corporate general partner, are personally exposed to criminal prosecution, joint unlimited civil liability for partnership debts under the Law of 10 August 1915, travel bans and exit interdictions in tax enforcement proceedings, and disqualification from holding management positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Letterbox SCSp with no staff or office, circular loan arrangements, back-to-back financing, management exercised wholly from abroad, no commercial rationale beyond tax avoidance, or treaty shopping through the transparent vehicle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under Art. 6 ACI with denial of fiscal transparency; reclassification of distributions as hidden dividends subject to 15% Luxembourg WHT; upward assessment at the 24.94% composite rate; 10% late-payment penalty and 0.6% monthly default interest; denial of DTA benefits; possible requalification of the SCSp as a taxable resident entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner may be jointly assessed for all unpaid taxes if the arrangement is held to constitute an abuse of law; criminal liability for aiding and abetting tax evasion; seizure of personal assets and enforceable travel bans during recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) within 30 days of incorporation or any change, filing false UBO data, or failing to maintain a know-your-partner file for the fund's investors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions under the RBE law: fines from EUR 500 to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 3 months per offence; additional fines under the AML Law of 12 November 2004 up to EUR 5,000,000 for regulated professionals; freezing of distributions and suspension of bank account operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner are individually liable for UBO compliance; convictions produce personal fines, imprisonment, and management disqualification; banks may terminate the SPV's accounts, causing payment defaults and triggering wrongful-trading claims against the directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's length interest on acquisition finance, excessive management or advisory fees to the private equity manager, unfounded guarantee fees, thin capitalization beyond the arm's length standard, or absence of contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment under Art. 56 LIR and Circular 56/1: recharacterization of excess interest or fees as hidden profit distributions; disallowance of the deduction; additional tax at 24.94% plus 10% penalty and 0.6% monthly default interest; aggravated penalty of up to 100% of the understated tax in cases of gross negligence; referral of the adjustment to the partner's home tax authority under exchange of information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partner directors may incur personal liability for wrongful trading (action en complement du passif) if the adjustment renders the SCSp unable to pay its creditors; criminal sanctions for participation in tax evasion; travel restrictions and personal asset attachment in the enforcement phase.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeated failure to file Form 541 and allocation schedules, persistent late payment of prepayments, or refusal to disclose partner identities to the ACD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 155 LIR surcharge of 10% of assessed tax; coercive fines up to EUR 2,500 per default; default interest at 0.6% per month; aggravated administrative penalty of up to 100% under Art. 1757 AO in cases of repeated willful default.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability of the general partner for the full tax claim; directors may face personal attachment orders and bank seizure of their private assets; arrest and travel bans may be ordered; professional disqualification follows a criminal conviction.
